correctness.rationale: Under the canonical finite-dimensional isometry ell_p² ⊗_ε ell_q² ≅ L(ell_{p′}²,ell_q²), the two-coordinate tensor corner is isometrically included for any m,n≥2, over real or complex scalars. If s=1/p+1/q≤1, p′≤q; identity I and sign D are norm-one maps and I±D are twice coordinate projections of norm two. For s>1, q<p′; I and swap S both have norm 2^(s−1) by exact two-coordinate ell_r norm comparisons, whereas I+S and I−S are rank-one operators of norm 2^s by Hölder. After scaling, both operators have norm one and their sum/difference both attain norm two, giving quotient C_NJ≥2 in the defining expression. Universal C_NJ≤2 proves equality. Endpoints p,q∈{1,∞}, s=1, m,n=2 and complex phases require no limiting argument. The high-dimensional identity follows from norm-one coordinate projections/inclusions.
